reaction: The clarification that early life did not need oxygen makes the change more interesting.

reason: Adding sediment seems the direct next step toward recording the sea's change.

effect: Banded iron completed the sea record and revealed a goal to shield life from ultraviolet light.

reason: Oxygen added to air seems the most direct route toward an atmospheric shield.

alternatives.reason: I considered exploring oxygen's effect on cells, but want to pursue the new shield goal first.

reason: Light acting on the oxygen-rich sky seems the clearest route toward the ultraviolet shield.
expectation: I expect an ozone layer or a step toward one, though the exact result is uncertain.

effect: Sheltered microbes completed the remaining goal, showing how oxygen-free life can persist in pockets beneath living layers and sediments.

mostWorthwhile.text: Building the oxygen-rich sky was most worthwhile: the revelation that a change helpful to some life could be deadly to other organisms gave the world's development meaningful consequences.

leastWorthwhile.text: Making the rusted seabed was comparatively thin on its own; the following banded-iron explanation made the geological connection much clearer.

surprise.text: Combining oxygen-using cells with a living cell produced a partnership rather than the contrast I expected. The endosymbiosis explanation was intriguing and candid about the compression.

arbitrary.text: The partnered-cells combination was not clearly connected to the remaining goal when I chose it, although the result explained its biological inspiration.

continue.text: Yes. I would be curious to see what the partnered cells become and how the world changes next; the oxygen crisis and its refuges made the unfolding story compelling.
